violationHarness.instrument: a FILE, not a shell one-liner: scratchpad/p104violate.py. Each case mutates one file, runs the check that should catch it, asserts a NON-ZERO exit, restores the file, and asserts the restored bytes are IDENTICAL to the pre-mutation bytes and the check passes again. A case that did not go 0 then non-zero then 0 is reported as harness failure, not as a proof.
violationHarness.selfCheckThatCaughtAHarnessDefect: First run aborted on case 1 with 'anchor count=0'. Cause: line endings are MIXED in this tree (core.autocrlf=true; pe-site-plan-export-core.ts and ReportsTool.tsx are CRLF in the working copy, the rest LF), so a \n-written anchor matched zero times. Had the harness not counted its anchor it would have silently no-opped and reported ten passes. The count check is the reason this is trustworthy. Fixed by translating each anchor into the target file's own newline convention.

instrumentGap.dispositionAndWhy: NOT ARMED BY THIS LANE. Adding the step to the workflow today would make CI permanently red on three pre-existing errors, which is DEV_PROCESS 2.0's dead-gate failure mode: a gate nobody can get to green gets ignored, and the bypass becomes the habit. Two of the three errors sit in files adjacent to other live lanes. Routed as a backlog item with the arming step written out. P-104's own type claim is verified by baseline-compare instead: 3 errors before, 3 after, and 4 under the deliberate violation.
